title.en: missing_capability: what an appliance cannot do, and what accepted means when a person does the rest

goal.en: A device that lacks an operation is refused alone and named at the first missing step. With a person present every missing step is assigned to the person, so accepted means a plan exists, not that the appliance does much of it.

note.en: The oven cannot grate an onion: refused at n1 with the reason spelled out.

expect.refusal.detail: device cannot perform cw.op.grate and no person is present to do it

note.en: The counter arm washes and drains the rice, then cannot heat a pan: two steps planned, refused at n3.
With a person: accepted. The person grates, cuts, mixes and forms; the oven preheats and bakes.
A salad on an oven with a person present is also accepted, and every one of the nine steps is the person's. Read the plan, not only the state.

outcome.en: You know how to read a missing_capability refusal and why a product page should count the steps the device does, not the recipes it accepts. Next: scenario 030 shows the refusal no person can lift.
